quotes.text: If the system cannot refuse a bad decision, you are not running governance. You are running persuasion, and persuasion does not scale.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines governance as the platform's ability to refuse, not to persuade.

quotes.text: The missing object is always the same. A decision owner with authority and obligation. Awareness without obligation is trivia. Obligation without authority is cruelty.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Pinpoints why dashboards alone fail: ownership needs both obligation and authority.

quotes.text: Governance is not the document you publish. Governance is what the platform will and will not allow. The PDF is theater. The control plane is real.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable reframing of governance as enforced intent.

quotes.text: A budget is the organization saying if spend crosses this line someone must respond in a defined time window with a defined set of options and a defined escalation path if they don't.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Turns budgets from finance documents into escalation contracts.

quotes.text: If an exception does not expire, it is not an exception. It is a new baseline you were too polite to name.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the single governance decision that prevents most drift.

chapters.title: Failure modes: dashboards, exceptions, shadow subscriptions
Three systems of action and ownership
Azure Policy, budgets, workflows and quarantine

takeaways: Showback creates visibility but no accountability; governance needs owners with authority, enforced constraints and an audit trail.
Combine guardrails (Azure Policy with mandatory owner and cost center tags), alarms (budgets as escalation contracts) and actuation (workflows that force a recorded decision).
Make exceptions expire by default and quarantine unowned resources, then measure unowned inventory, exception age and time to decision instead of savings.
hook: Cost dashboards make organizations feel in control while cloud and Microsoft 365 spend keeps drifting. This episode shows FinOps, platform and finance leaders why showback is not accountability and how guardrails, budget escalation, workflow automation and expiring exceptions turn visibility into real cost ownership.
